name: Barbell Squat
instructions: Set the bar on a rack at upper-chest height and load it evenly. Step under it so it rests across your upper traps, not your neck.
Grip the bar just outside shoulder width, unrack it, and take two controlled steps back. Set feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Take a big breath, brace your core, and sit down and back as if lowering into a chair.
Descend until your hip crease drops below the top of your knees, keeping your chest tall and knees tracking over your toes.
Drive through your whole foot to stand back up, exhaling near the top. Lock out hips and knees together.
formTip: Keep your weight centered over mid-foot. If your heels lift or you tip forward, drop the load and rebuild.

name: Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on the bench with eyes under the bar and feet planted firmly on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and squeeze your shoulder blades down and together.
Unrack the bar and hold it over your chest with arms straight.
Lower the bar under control to the middle of your chest, keeping elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle to your torso.
Press the bar back up in a slight arc toward your face until your arms lock out.
formTip: Drive your feet into the floor and keep your glutes on the bench. Full-body tension makes the press stronger and safer.

name: Deadlift
instructions: Stand with mid-foot under the barbell, feet hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips and grip the bar just outside your knees, arms straight.
Drop your hips, lift your chest, and pull the slack out of the bar so your lats engage.
Brace hard, then drive through the floor and stand tall, keeping the bar dragging close to your legs.
Lock out by squeezing your glutes, then reverse the motion under control to set the bar down.
formTip: Keep the bar touching your body the entire lift. A bar that drifts forward rounds your back and kills your leverage.

name: Overhead Press
instructions: Set the bar at your front shoulders, hands just outside shoulder width, elbows pointing forward.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and brace your core and glutes.
Press the bar straight up, moving your head back slightly to clear a path.
Once the bar passes your forehead, push your head through so the bar finishes stacked over your mid-foot.
Lock out overhead, then lower under control back to your shoulders.
formTip: Squeeze your glutes and pull your ribs down before pressing. This stops you leaning back and turning it into an incline press.

name: Pull Up
instructions: Grip the bar with palms facing away, hands just wider than shoulders.
Hang with arms fully extended, then pull your shoulder blades down and back to start.
Drive your elbows down toward your ribs and pull your chest to the bar.
Lift until your chin clears the bar, keeping your core tight to avoid swinging.
Lower under control all the way back to a full hang before the next rep.
formTip: Lead with your chest, not your chin. Think about pulling your elbows into your back pockets.

name: Dumbbell Row
instructions: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a bench, back flat and roughly parallel to the floor.
Hold the dumbbell in your free hand with your arm hanging straight down.
Brace your core and pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, leading with your elbow.
Squeeze your back at the top with the dumbbell near your lower ribs.
Lower under control to a full stretch, then repeat before switching sides.
formTip: Keep your torso still and rotation-free. The row comes from your back, not from twisting your body.

name: Lunge
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips or at your sides.
Take a controlled step forward into a comfortable stride.
Lower straight down until both knees are bent to about 90 degrees, front shin vertical.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee tracking over your toes.
Push through your front heel to return to standing, then alternate legs.
formTip: Drop straight down, not forward. Your front knee should stay stacked over your ankle, not shoot past your toes.

name: Push Up
instructions: Start in a high plank with hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in a straight line.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your hips do not sag.
Bend your elbows to about 45 degrees and lower your chest toward the floor.
Descend until your chest is just above the ground.
Press back up powerfully until your arms are straight, keeping your body rigid throughout.
formTip: Keep your body one straight line from head to heels. No sagging hips, no piked hips.

name: Plank
instructions: Set your forearms on the floor with elbows directly under your shoulders.
Extend your legs behind you and rise onto your toes.
Form a straight line from head to heels and brace your core hard.
Squeeze your glutes and quads and keep breathing steadily.
Hold the position for time without letting your hips drop or pike.
formTip: Actively pull your elbows toward your toes and tuck your ribs down. A plank is an active brace, not a passive hang.

name: Bicep Curl
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides, palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides and your upper arms still.
Curl the weights up by bending only at the elbow.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top without swinging.
Lower under control until your arms are fully straight, then repeat.
formTip: If your elbows drift forward or you rock your torso, the weight is too heavy. Strict reps build the biceps.

name: Tricep Extension
instructions: Attach a rope or bar to a high cable pulley and grip it with both hands.
Stand tall, tuck your elbows to your sides, and start with your forearms parallel to the floor.
Keeping your upper arms locked in place, extend your forearms down until your arms are straight.
Squeeze your triceps hard at the bottom of the movement.
Slowly return to the start, letting your forearms rise without moving your elbows.
formTip: Your elbows are the hinge. Pin them to your ribs so every rep isolates the triceps, not your shoulders.

name: Leg Press
instructions: Sit in the machine with your back flat against the pad and feet shoulder-width on the platform.
Release the safety handles and hold the platform with legs nearly straight, keeping a soft knee.
Lower the platform under control until your knees reach about 90 degrees.
Keep your lower back and hips glued to the seat throughout.
Drive through your whole foot to press the platform back up without locking your knees hard.
formTip: Do not let your lower back round off the seat at the bottom. Stop the descent before your hips tuck under.

name: Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit at the machine and grip the bar wider than shoulder width, palms facing away.
Secure your thighs under the pad and lean back very slightly.
Pull the bar down toward your upper chest, driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom.
Return the bar under control to a full stretch overhead before the next rep.
formTip: Lead with your elbows and keep your chest proud. Avoid yanking the bar with just your arms.

name: Seated Row
instructions: Sit facing the cable with feet braced and a slight bend in your knees.
Grab the handle, sit tall, and extend your arms with a light stretch in your back.
Pull the handle toward your belly, driving your elbows straight back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and keep your torso upright.
Extend your arms back out under control, keeping your chest tall throughout.
formTip: Move from your back, not your lower spine. Keep your torso still rather than rocking for momentum.

name: Face Pull
instructions: Set a rope on a cable pulley at roughly face height and grip both ends with thumbs back.
Step back to create tension and stand tall with arms extended.
Pull the rope toward your face, flaring the ends apart as you go.
Drive your elbows high and squeeze your rear delts and upper back.
Return the rope under control to the starting stretch.
formTip: Aim the rope at your forehead and finish with your hands beside your ears. High elbows hit the rear delts best.

name: Calf Raise
instructions: Stand with the balls of your feet on the machine platform, heels hanging off the edge.
Rise up under the pad or load and stand tall with a slight knee bend.
Lower your heels below the platform for a full stretch in your calves.
Press up onto your toes as high as possible.
Squeeze at the top for a beat, then lower slowly under control.
formTip: Use a full range. A deep stretch at the bottom and a hard squeeze at the top beats short, bouncy reps.

name: Hamstring Curl
instructions: Lie face down on the machine with the pad resting just above your heels.
Grip the handles and keep your hips pressed into the bench.
Curl your heels toward your glutes by contracting your hamstrings.
Squeeze hard at the top without lifting your hips off the pad.
Lower under control until your legs are nearly straight, then repeat.
formTip: Keep your hips down. If they pop up, you are using your lower back instead of your hamstrings.

name: Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing in.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows and brace your core.
Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until they reach shoulder height.
Lead with your elbows and keep your wrists level with your hands.
Lower under control back to your sides without swinging.
formTip: Keep the movement slow and lead with the elbows. Momentum steals the tension from your side delts.

name: Box Jump
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy box a comfortable distance away, feet hip-width apart.
Hinge slightly and swing your arms back to load.
Explode upward by driving your arms up and extending your hips.
Land softly on the box with both feet flat and knees bent to absorb the impact.
Stand fully upright on the box, then step down one foot at a time to reset.
formTip: Step down, do not jump down. Repeated hard landings off the box beat up your knees for no extra benefit.

name: Burpee
instructions: Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
Drop into a squat and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Kick your feet back into a high plank and lower your chest to the floor.
Press up and hop your feet back toward your hands.
Explode straight up into a jump with arms overhead, then land soft and repeat.
formTip: Keep a braced core as you kick out and pace your breathing so form holds up as fatigue sets in.
